explanation: Fires almost entirely (99.5% of mass) during the original input phase, at orig_idx 3-8 (peak 4-6), never at t<2 and essentially never in the copy phase (small residue at <DEL>). The input token must be from a group led by l, k, y, n, v (then r, j, a, h, 2, c, i), usually its first occurrence (in_first carries 90% of mass). Firing depends on context: it is strongest when the earlier prefix holds many tokens from a second group (z, 0, w, b, m, u, s, d, q; first_tok z/0/w/b has 3-4x lift), and it can fire on several B-group tokens in a row after such a prefix (top examples: 0 w w e w s 2 [l]; b b b b v l y [l]). The same B-group tokens after a prefix that already contains B-group tokens or other letters often do not fire, so the neuron behaves like a graded linear readout of prefix composition, not a crisp rule. Predicate: B-group token, first occurrence, with at least 3 A-group tokens earlier. Dev F1 is about 0.36 (precision 0.31, recall 0.44, mass recall 0.53). Looser versions (any B token at t>=3) reach 98% recall at 9% precision.
